Generator

Texture view preserves the uploaded image. Volume adds animated depth using its colors and brightness. Use PNG, density, or RFL system export; editable C recipes support procedural presets only.

Beams reach 1 light-year per side by default, then fade through orange lobes and purple backscatter out to about 7.7 light-years. Adjust Beam length in Stars. Zoom in to inspect the rough gas torus and central object; their sizes are enlarged for visibility.

Comet tail

Knots and separated filaments stream away from the star. Drag the volume to inspect depth; change the star direction to turn the whole tail.

Lengths are preview proportions. AU controls the scorched-world cutoff. Hot Jupiters will follow comet validation.

Tiling applies to Texture mode. Volume mode uses the selected 3D shape.

18 stars · 5 jet sources

Each colored star carves a spherical clearing. Jet sources emit two long opposing beams, ending in orange lobes with purple backscatter. Look down either jet to see a dithered glare; rotate away to reveal the cones. Spread moves stars into and around the nebula.

Blue reflection after 3 s; bright green ionization after 6 s, beginning near the jet tips. Each region returns to blue after four seconds, then the nova slowly dims to half brightness.

About this generator

Volume mode ray-marches an animated 3D density field in C. Rotation reveals depth through the gas, stars, spherical clearings, and jets. Texture mode retains the original flat generator. Motion is a procedural visual approximation, not a hydrodynamic simulation.

PNG exports capture the current frame with transparency, including the modeled stars and jets but excluding the distant preview starfield. Volume density exports contain the integrated gas column for the current view; Texture exports contain the original 2D field. Pause motion for a still composition.

Comets are animated 3D density fields inspired by the supplied photographs: a green-white coma, separated blue or cyan filaments, flowing knots, and a fading outer haze. Star bearing and elevation determine the anti-stellar direction; camera rotation never changes it. The scorched-planet variant uses a straight yellow sodium tail originating across the full planetary diameter at 0.387 AU or closer. Density flows outward along fixed anti-stellar streamlines; the tail never bends or wags. This is an artistic eligibility rule; hot Jupiters are deferred. RFL export bakes the current direction, so runtime attachment to an orbiting body requires the game to orient the volume away from its star.

Nova B lights scattered clouds in a detached shell just beyond the jet tips. Hydrogen ejecta use a separate warm palette. Jets emerge from the flash and reach full length at five seconds. Blue reflection starts at three seconds; bright green ionization starts at six seconds along both jet directions and spreads through the clouds. Each region returns to blue four seconds after the green arrives; total nova brightness fades to half from 16 to 46 seconds. Changing beam length also moves the shell to preserve the gap. Dark tadpole globules and branching pillars catch blue rims as the echo passes. This is a time-compressed visual model. Replay restarts the flash; Randomize changes the cloud.

Nova holds a red point, grows a Noctis-style dithered glare, then releases a nebula around a flickering blue-white remnant. The gas cutoff increases from 0.15 to 0.47 over the expansion, while the clearing radius grows from 0.12 to 0.28 at half that rate. The clearing then holds at its maximum while the shell continues expanding slowly until 60 seconds after the flash. Jet cones have a 50% chance per seed. Replay repeats the same event; Randomize starts a new one.
